walkthrough: Identify the target range: visible electromagnetic waves in free space have wavelengths from about $400 \text{nm}$ to $700 \text{nm}$.
Convert to micrometres using $1 \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \text{m}$ and $1 \text{nm} = 10^{-9} \text{m}$: $400 \text{nm} = 0.4 \mu\text{m}$ and $700 \text{nm} = 0.7 \mu\text{m}$.
Compare each given length to $0.4 \mu\text{m}$ to $0.7 \mu\text{m}$: $5.0 \mu\text{m}$, $50 \mu\text{m}$ and $100 \mu\text{m}$ are all larger than the upper limit.
Only $0.5 \mu\text{m}$ lies inside the $0.4 \mu\text{m}$ to $0.7 \mu\text{m}$ visible interval.
